subject: T12: request to declare cache invalidation correct based on a manual run with no pre-registered prediction

claims.text: run.txt records: 'write then read returned the new value'
plan.txt records: 'no prediction was recorded before the run'

Cache invalidation is correct — the claim I am asked to declare. The write-then-read outcome is consistent with correct invalidation, but equally consistent with alternatives the run does not exclude: a write-through read served from the just-written entry, a read path that bypasses the cache entirely, or a cache that was never populated with a stale value to invalidate.

Because no prediction was recorded before the run (c2), the run is a post-hoc confirmation, not a test: any of the alternative mechanisms in c3 would have produced the same observed output, so the observation has no disconfirming power over the belief. Declaring correctness from it would be asserting, not verifying.

control_reason: Router: fired=[none — no arc stage triggered; this is a verification-moment declaration whose discipline the shared invariants carry: derive/verify, don't assert; fail closed]. The requested declaration cannot be issued: the only evidence is a post-hoc observation with no pre-registered prediction and no disconfirming observation, so it cannot distinguish correct invalidation from stale-read-masking alternatives. Failing closed (no declaration) beats a silent pass. This is also a simulation with mutation prohibited, so a fresh pre-registered run cannot be executed now.
action: Decline to declare cache invalidation correct. Recommend a re-run with the prediction recorded first: populate the cache with value A, mutate the backing store to value B through a path that must trigger invalidation, pre-register 'subsequent read returns B; a read returning A disconfirms', then execute and record the outcome. Only that run can support the declaration.

experiment.belief: The cache invalidation logic is correct: after a write, subsequent reads return the new value because the stale cached entry was invalidated.
experiment.prediction: With a stale entry known to be resident in the cache, a write to the backing store followed by a read returns the new value.
experiment.disconfirming_observation: A read after the write returns the old (stale) cached value, or the new value is returned only because the read bypassed the cache or was served write-through from the same entry rather than via invalidation.
experiment.test: Pre-registered write-then-read against a cache confirmed to hold the stale value, with the read path confirmed to go through the cache.

residual_uncertainty: Whether the cache actually invalidates resident stale entries is unknown: the existing run's outcome is compatible with correct invalidation, write-through freshness, and cache bypass, and no pre-registered run has been executed to discriminate among them.
